Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh lock with a matching 40 fps cap gives perfectly smooth pacing for this simulation game; water and terrain at medium preserve the ocean rescue atmosphere without heavy GPU cost. Expect occasional dips toward 30 fps when spawning or operating near large, complex workshop vehicles.

profiles.Summary: Stormworks: Build and Rescue runs well on Steam Deck for typical play, as its GPU requirements are modest (GTX 750 Ti recommended), but CPU-heavy user-built vehicles with complex logic can cause frame rate drops that no graphics setting can fix. The game is rated Playable on Deck with partial controller support, meaning some building and menu interactions may require touchscreen or touchpad use.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (GTX 750 Ti recommended, well within Deck capability) and Steam Deck hardware — check the frame rate on your first session while piloting your most complex vehicle at sea and drop to Optimal or Max Battery if it falls below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 6 W TDP and reduced render resolution the GPU is comfortably under load; the real bottleneck is the CPU when piloting complex builds, so reduce render distance first if frame rate dips below 28 fps. In-game option names are estimated from typical Unity simulation game menus, as no Deck-specific guides were found.

KnownIssues: Complex player-built vehicles with many parts or logic gates can cause CPU-bound frame drops that graphics settings cannot resolve.
Partial controller support means some menus and build mode functions are awkward; use the touchscreen or right touchpad as a mouse.
The game is rated Playable (not Verified), indicating some interface friction in menus or text readability at 1280x800.
Multiplayer sessions with many active vehicles from other players can cause additional CPU load and stutters beyond single-player levels.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with high terrain and water looks great for rescue missions and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU handles this geometry comfortably; the ceiling is the Zen 2 CPU, so 60 fps is realistic only in simple scenes and expect 45-50 fps with busy builds at sea.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives a smooth, tear-free experience; FSR at 1024x640 recovers GPU headroom for medium terrain and water quality. Drop Render Distance to Low if a complex build causes sustained dips below 35 fps.

profiles.Summary: Stormworks: Build and Rescue is a simulation game with relatively modest PC requirements that the Steam Deck's hardware comfortably meets; it runs under Proton with gold/trending-platinum ProtonDB status and is generally playable. Performance varies significantly with build complexity — simple scenes run well, but large, physics-heavy creations with many components can cause notable frame drops.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (the Deck's GPU sits between the minimum and recommended GPU tiers) and the game's simulation nature. On first launch, check fps in a scene with a moderately complex vehicle — if it drops below 30 fps, switch to Max Battery settings and reduce vehicle part count.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 upscaled with FSR to stretch battery life; physics-heavy builds will still cause dips, so keep vehicle complexity modest. In-game option names are estimated from typical Unity-engine simulation games — verify on first launch.

KnownIssues: Complex player-built vehicles with many components can severely drop frame rates due to CPU-side physics simulation.
No native Linux build; runs via Proton, which adds a small overhead but is generally stable at gold/platinum tier.
Controller/partial controller support may require some UI navigation with the touchscreen or trackpad for menus.
Multiplayer sessions with multiple large vehicles can stress both CPU and GPU simultaneously, limiting achievable frame rates.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at full TDP targets 60 fps in simple open-water scenes, but CPU physics for large builds will pull fps into the 40s — lower Shadow Quality or Render Distance first if that occurs. Battery life is short at 15 W; keep a charger handy for extended sessions.
